paragraphs: Unless otherwise indicated or the context otherwise requires, references in this "Item 1. Business" section to "the combined company," "we," "us" and other similar terms refer to Alpha Metallurgical Resources, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries (previously Contura Energy, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries). Certain terms that are used throughout this Annual Report on Form 10-K but not otherwise defined are defined under the "Glossary" herein. Disclosures in this "Item 1. Business" section should be read in conjunction with "Item 1A. Risk Factors" for further discussion of factors impacting our business.

We are a Tennessee-based mining company with operations in Virginia and West Virginia. With customers across the globe, high-quality reserves and significant port capacity, we reliably supply metallurgical coal products to the steel industry. We operate highly productive, cost-competitive coal mines across the CAPP coal basin. Our portfolio of mining operations consists of 14 active underground mines, five active surface mines and eight active coal preparation plants, as well as one underground mine, one surface mine, and one coal preparation plant that have been temporarily idled. We own a 65.0% interest in Dominion Terminal Associates ("DTA"), a coal export terminal in Newport News, Virginia. DTA provides us with the ability to fulfill a broad range of customer coal quality requirements through coal blending, while also providing storage capacity and transportation flexibility.

We predominantly produce metallurgical ("met") coal, which is shipped to domestic and international steel and coke producers. Although our strategic focus is on the production of met coal, we also produce thermal coal as byproduct and it is primarily sold to large utilities and industrial customers both in the United States and across the world. Refer to Notes 21 and 22 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for geographical information about our coal sales and additional segment information.

We have a substantial reserve base of 294.5 million tons of proven and probable reserves as of December 31, 2025. Our reserve base consists of 282.8 million tons of proven and probable metallurgical reserves, and 11.7 million tons of proven and probable thermal reserves.

Through our operations, we are able to source coal from multiple mines to meet the needs of a long-standing global customer base, many of which have been served by us or our predecessors for decades. We are continuously evaluating opportunities to strategically cultivate current relationships to drive new business in our target growth markets. In addition, our experienced management team regularly analyzes potential acquisitions, joint ventures and other opportunities that would be accretive and synergistic to our existing asset portfolio.

In 2025, due to continued softness in the met coal pricing environment, especially for U.S. High-Vol. products driven by weak global steel demand combined with additional U.S. High-Vol. production, we reduced production levels at our Jerry Fork and Black Eagle mines within our Power Mountain and Marfork mining complexes, respectively, and temporarily idled our Long Branch surface mine within our McClure/Toms Creek mining complex. For more information refer to "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

In 2024, we began the development phase for our new Kingston Wildcat underground mine located in Fayette County, West Virginia. The mine, which will produce a Low-Vol. quality met coal, is expected to begin production in the first quarter of 2026.

In November 2024, due to a softening in the met coal pricing environment, we temporarily idled our Elk Run mining complex. Its Checkmate Powellton mine, which had recently begun production and had not yet reached planned production levels, had relatively higher costs. The mine is being maintained and is expected to be restarted once market conditions improve.

In 2023, we completed development of and commenced production at our Rolling Thunder and Checkmate Powellton mines within our Power Mountain and Elk Run mining complexes, respectively, which produce High-Vol. B quality met coal
from the Powellton coal seam. Our History
We were formed in 2016 to acquire and operate certain of Alpha Natural Resources, Inc.'s former core coal operations, as part of the Alpha Natural Resources, Inc. Plan of Reorganization.

On November 9, 2018, we merged with Alpha Natural Resources Holdings, Inc. and ANR, Inc. Upon the consummation of the transactions contemplated by a definitive merger agreement (the "Merger Agreement"), our common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "CTRA." Previously, our shares traded on the OTC market under the ticker "CNTE."

On December 10, 2020, we closed on a transaction with Iron Senergy Holdings, LLC, to sell our thermal coal mining operations located in Pennsylvania consisting primarily of our Cumberland mining complex and related property (our former NAPP operations). This transaction accelerated our strategic exit from thermal coal production to shift our focus to met coal production.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Industry and the Global Economy
Declines in coal prices and/or sustained low prices would adversely affect our revenues, operating results, cash flows, financial condition, stock price and the value of our coal reserves.
The concurrent loss of, or significant reduction in, purchases by several of our largest customers could materially and adversely affect our revenues and profitability.
Competition within the coal industry may adversely affect our ability to sell coal, and excess production capacity in the industry could put downward pressure on coal prices.
Our ability to collect payments from our customers could be impaired if their creditworthiness and financial health deteriorate.
Risks Relating to Regulatory and Legal Developments
Our operations may impact the environment or cause exposure to hazardous substances, and our properties may have environmental contamination, which could result in material liabilities to us.
The increasingly stringent regulation of the mining industry imposes significant costs on us, and future regulations or violations could increase those costs or limit our ability to produce coal.
Increasing attention to environmental, social and governance ("ESG") matters may negatively affect our business and financial results.
Climate change or carbon dioxide emissions reduction initiatives could significantly reduce the demand for coal and reduce the value of our coal assets.

We may be unable to obtain and renew permits, mine plan modifications and approvals, leases or other rights necessary for our operations, which would reduce our production, cash flows and profitability.

Our systems and procedures for internal control over financial reporting or the disclosure controls related to them may in the future have material weaknesses, which may adversely affect the value of our common stock.
Certain U.S. federal income tax provisions currently available with respect to coal percentage depletion and exploration and development may be eliminated by future legislation.
Changes in tax laws, in the areas of both income taxes and non-income taxes, may materially affect our results of operations and could cause our financial position and profitability to deteriorate.

Disruptions in transportation services or port facilities, and increased transportation costs, could impair our ability to supply coal to our customers, reduce demand and adversely affect our business.
Expenditures for certain employee benefits could be materially higher than we have anticipated, which could increase our costs and adversely affect our financial results.
Our business requires substantial capital investment and maintenance expenditures, which we may be unable to provide.
paragraphs: Investment in our securities is subject to various risks, including risks and uncertainties inherent in our business. As detailed in the following pages, these risks include, but are not limited to, the following:

•Risks relating to our industry and the global economy, such as those associated with low coal prices, loss of customers, tariffs and other trade restrictions, our ability to obtain financing and other services, competition, decreased demand for coal, customer creditworthiness and global economic disruptions.

•Risks relating to regulatory and legal developments, such as those associated with regulatory requirements and costs, healthcare regulations and costs, permit approvals, climate change regulations, social and governance initiatives and regulations, environmental laws and treaties, unfavorable tax actions, decreased demand for energy, environmental cleanup costs and maintenance of internal controls.

•Risks relating to our operations, such as those associated with mining and other conditions, many of which are beyond our control, disruptions in transportation services, the availability of skilled workers, higher than estimated employee benefit costs, the availability of coal reserves, equipment availability, equipment breakdown, higher than anticipated property reclamation or mine closure costs, unionization, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, the complexity of mining in Central Appalachia, our dependence upon third parties and our ability to make capital investments.

•Risks relating to our liquidity, such as our ability to obtain or renew surety bonds, our need to maintain capacity for required letters of credit ("LCs"), limitations imposed on us by our borrowing arrangements or any future debt instruments and access to funds when needed.

•Risks relating to the ownership of our common stock, such as those associated with compliance with securities laws, the availability of an orderly trading market for our common stock, our ability to repurchase common shares, as the Board may determine from time to time, dilution or other effects resulting from the issuance of additional securities, impediments to our acquisition by a third party and limited fora for stockholder litigation matters.

paragraphs: We are a Tennessee-based mining company with operations across Virginia and West Virginia. With customers across the globe, high-quality reserves and significant port capacity, we are a leading supplier of metallurgical coal products to the steel industry. We operate high-quality, cost-competitive coal mines across the CAPP coal basin. As of December 31, 2025, our operations consisted of nineteen active mines and eight active coal preparation and load-out facilities, with approximately 3,960 employees. We produce, process, and sell met coal and thermal coal. We also sell coal produced by others, some of which is processed and/or blended with coal produced from our mines prior to resale, with the remainder purchased for resale. As of December 31, 2025, we had 294.5 million tons of reserves, which included 282.8 million tons of proven and probable metallurgical reserves and 11.7 million tons of proven and probable thermal reserves.

We began operations on July 26, 2016, with mining operations in NAPP, CAPP, and the PRB. Through the Acquisition, we acquired a significant reserve base. We also acquired Alpha Natural Resources Inc.'s 40.6% interest in the DTA coal export terminal in Newport News, Virginia, and on March 31, 2017, we acquired a portion of another partner's ownership stake and increased our interest to 65.0%. We merged with Alpha Natural Resources Holdings, Inc. and ANR, Inc. on November 9, 2018.

On December 10, 2020, we closed on a transaction with Iron Senergy Holdings, LLC, to sell our thermal coal mining operations located in Pennsylvania consisting primarily of our Cumberland mining complex and related property (our former NAPP operations). This transaction accelerated our strategic exit from thermal coal production to shift our focus to met coal production.

For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, sales of met coal were 14.1 million tons and 15.9 million tons, respectively, and accounted for approximately 93% and 93%, respectively, of our coal sales volume. Sales of thermal coal were 1.2 million tons and 1.2 million tons, respectively, and accounted for approximately 7% and 7%, respectively, of our coal sales volume.

Our sales of met coal were made primarily in several countries in Asia, Europe, and the Americas and to steel companies in the northeastern and midwestern regions of the United States. Our sales of thermal coal were made primarily to large utilities and industrial customers both in the United States and across the world. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 approximately 73% and 78%, respectively, of our coal revenues were derived from coal sales made to customers outside the United States.

In addition, we generate other revenues from equipment sales, rentals, terminal and processing fees, coal and environmental analysis fees, royalties and the sale of natural gas. We also record freight and handling fulfillment revenue within coal revenues for freight and handling services provided in delivering coal to certain customers, which are a component of the contractual selling price.

As of December 31, 2025, we have one reportable operating segment: Met. Refer to Notes 21 and 22 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional disclosures on our reportable segment, geographic areas, and export coal revenue information.

As discussed in the "Market Overview" presented above, metallurgical coal prices remain at lower levels than in recent years due to weak global steel demand which has been influenced by a slowdown in manufacturing activity. Economic pressures, geopolitical uncertainty, and shifting trade policies have contributed to metallurgical market challenges. Our results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 were impacted by these factors.

paragraphs: 除非另有說明或上下文另有要求，本項 "業務" 項目中提及 "合併公司"、"我們"、"我們" 及其他類似詞彙，均指 Alpha Metallurgical Resources, Inc. 及其合併子公司（先前為 Contura Energy, Inc. 及其合併子公司）。本年度 10-K 報告中使用但未另行定義的某些詞彙，於本處 "詞彙表" 中定義。本項 "業務" 項目中的揭露應與 "項 1A. 風險因素" 一併閱讀，以進一步討論影響我們業務的因素。

我們是一家位於田納西州的採礦公司，營運範圍涵蓋維吉尼亞州與西維吉尼亞州。我們擁有全球客戶羣、高品質儲備與大量港口容量，可可靠地供應冶金煤產品給鋼鐵產業。我們在 CAPP 煤礦盆地內運營高產且成本競爭力的煤礦。我們的採礦業務組合包含 14 座活躍的地下礦場、5 座活躍的露天礦場與 8 座活躍的煤處理廠，以及 1 座地下礦場、1 座露天礦場與 1 座煤處理廠暫時停工。我們擁有 Dominion Terminal Associates（"DTA"）65.0% 的權益，DTA 是位於維吉尼亞州 Newport News 的煤炭出口碼頭。DTA 讓我們有能力透過煤炭混合來滿足廣泛的客戶煤炭品質需求，同時也提供儲存空間與運輸靈活性。
我們主要生產冶金煤（"met" 煤），這些煤炭運送到國內與國際的鋼鐵與焦炭製造商。雖然我們的戰略重點在於生產冶金煤，但我們也會生產熱煤作為副產品，並主要銷售給美國與全球的大型電力與工業客戶。有關我們煤炭銷售的地理資訊與額外分部資訊，請參閱合併財務報表的附註 21 與 22。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有 294.5 百萬噸的已證實與可能儲備。我們的儲備包含 282.8 百萬噸的已證實與可能冶金煤儲備，以及 11.7 百萬噸的已證實與可能熱煤儲備。
透過我們的營運，我們能夠從多個礦場取得煤炭，以滿足長期的全球客戶需求，許多客戶已經由我們或我們的前身服務了數十年。我們持續評估機會，以戰略方式培養現有關係，推動我們目標成長市場的新業務。此外，我們經驗豐富的管理團隊定期分析潛在的併購、合資企業及其他機會，這些機會將對我們現有資產組合產生正面影響與協同效益。

2025 年，由於冶金煤價格環境持續疲軟，特別是美國高揮發性產品的價格，受到全球鋼鐵需求疲弱與美國高揮發性生產增加的影響，我們在 Power Mountain 與 Marfork 煤礦複合體內的 Jerry Fork 與 Black Eagle 煤礦減少了生產量，並暫時停工了 McClure/Toms Creek 煤礦複合體內的 Long Branch 露天礦場。如需更多資訊，請參閱 "項 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析與討論"。
2024 年，我們開始開發位於西維吉尼亞州 Fayette 縣的 Kingston Wildcat 地下礦場。該礦場將生產低揮發性品質的冶金煤，預計於 2026 年第一季開始生產。
2024 年 11 月，由於冶金煤價格環境趨緩，我們暫時停工了 Elk Run 煤礦複合體。其 Checkmate Powellton 煤礦最近開始生產，但尚未達到預期的生產水平，成本相對較高。該礦場目前維持運作，預計在市場條件改善後重新啟動。
2023 年，我們完成 Rolling Thunder 與 Checkmate Powellton 煤礦的開發，並開始在 Power Mountain 與 Elk Run 煤礦複合體內進行生產，這些煤礦生產 High-Vol. B 等級的冶金煤
來自 Powellton 煤層。我們的歷史
我們於 2016 年成立，旨在取得並運營 Alpha Natural Resources, Inc. 過去的核心燃煤業務，作為 Alpha Natural Resources, Inc. 重整計畫的一部分。
2018 年 11 月 9 日，我們與 Alpha Natural Resources Holdings, Inc. 及 ANR, Inc. 合併。根據一份最終合併協議（"合併協議"）所規範的交易完成後，我們的普通股開始在紐約證券交易所（New York Stock Exchange）交易，股票代碼為 "CTRA"。在此之前，我們的股票在 OTC 市場交易，股票代碼為 "CNTE."
2020 年 12 月 10 日，我們與 Iron Senergy Holdings, LLC 完成交易，出售位於賓夕法尼亞州的熱燃煤礦業務，主要包括 Cumberland 煤礦複合體及相關財產（我們過去的 NAPP 業務）。此交易加速我們從熱燃煤生產的戰略退出，轉而專注於冶金煤生產。

paragraphs: 本公司為位於田納西州的採礦公司，營運範圍遍及維吉尼亞州與西維吉尼亞州。擁有全球客戶羣、高品質儲備與顯著的港口容量，本公司為鋼鐵產業提供冶金煤產品的主要供應商。本公司在CAPP煤盆地內營運高品質、成本競爭力的煤礦。截至2025年12月31日，本公司營運範圍包括十九座活躍礦區與八座活躍的煤處理與裝載設施，約有3,960名員工。本公司生產、處理與銷售冶金煤與熱煤。本公司亦銷售由他人生產的煤，其中部分煤在重新銷售前已進行處理與/或與本公司礦區生產的煤混合，其餘則為購入後重新銷售。截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有294.5百萬噸儲備，其中包括282.8百萬噸已證實與或可能的冶金煤儲備，以及11.7百萬噸已證實與或可能的熱煤儲備。

本公司於2016年7月26日開始營運，營運範圍包括NAPP、CAPP與PRB地區。透過收購，本公司取得相當規模的儲備基礎。本公司亦取得Alpha Natural Resources Inc.在維吉尼亞州紐波特新聞的DTA煤出口碼頭40.6%的權益，並於2017年3月31日取得另一合作夥伴的部分股權，使本公司權益增加至65.0%。本公司於2018年11月9日與Alpha Natural Resources Holdings, Inc.及ANR, Inc.合併。
於2020年12月10日，本公司完成與Iron Senergy Holdings, LLC的交易，出售位於賓夕法尼亞州的熱煤採礦業務，主要為本公司 Cumberland採礦複合體及相關財產（本公司先前的NAPP業務）。此交易加速本公司從熱煤生產的戰略退出，轉而專注於冶金煤生產。
截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日，冶金煤銷售量分別為14.1百萬噸與15.9百萬噸，分別佔本公司煤銷售總量約93%與93%。熱煤銷售量分別為1.2百萬噸與1.2百萬噸，分別佔本公司煤銷售總量約7%與7%。
本公司冶金煤銷售主要在亞洲、歐洲與美洲的幾個國家，以及美國東北部與中西部地區的鋼鐵公司。本公司熱煤銷售主要為美國境內及全球的大型電力與工業客戶。截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日，本公司煤營收約有73%與78%來自於銷售給美國境外客戶的煤。
此外，本公司亦透過設備銷售、租金、碼頭與處理費用、煤與環境分析費用、特許權費及天然氣銷售產生其他收入。本公司亦在煤營收內記錄貨運與處理履行收入，用以反映為特定客戶交付煤所提供貨運與處理服務，此為契約銷售價格的組成部分。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司有一個應報告營運分部：冶金煤。請參閱財務報表附註第21及22項，以取得更多關於本公司應報告分部、地理區域及出口煤營收資訊的揭露。
如上文所述的「市場概觀」所討論，冶金煤價格仍低於近年水平，這是因全球鋼鐵需求疲軟所致，而此需求疲軟受到製造活動減緩的影響。經濟壓力、地緣政治不確定性與貿易政策變動已導致冶金煤市場面臨挑戰。本公司2025年12月31日財年營運結果受到這些因素的影響。

headings: 產業與全球經濟相關風險
煤價下跌或持續低價將不利於我們的營業收入、營運結果、現金流、財務狀況、股票價格以及煤礦儲備價值。
我們主要客戶中數個若同時失去或大幅減少採購，將可能對我們的營業收入與獲利能力造成重大且不利的影響。
煤產業內的競爭可能不利於我們銷售煤的能力，產業內過度的生產能力可能對煤價造成向下壓力。
若客戶的信用worthiness與財務狀況惡化，我們收取客戶付款的能力可能受到影響。
與監管及法律發展相關的風險
我們的營運可能影響環境或導致接觸有害物質，我們的資產可能有環境污染，這可能導致我們產生重大負債。
礦業日益嚴格的監管規定對我們造成重大成本，未來的監管措施或違規行為可能增加這些成本或限制我們生產煤的能力。
對環境、社會及治理（"ESG"）議題日益重視，可能會對我們的業務及財務結果產生負面影響。
氣候變遷或二氧化碳排放量減量措施，可能會顯著降低對燃煤的需求，並降低我們燃煤資產的價值。
我們可能無法取得並續約營運所需之許可證、礦區計畫變更與核准、租賃或其他權利，這將降低我們的產能、現金流及獲利能力。
我們用以控制財務報告之內部控制系統及相關資訊揭露控制程序，未來可能出現重大缺失，這可能會對我們普通股之價值產生負面影響。
美國聯邦所得稅法中目前針對燃煤百分比減損及探勘與開發之相關條款，未來可能因立法而被廢除。
所得稅及其他非所得稅法規之變更，可能會對我們營運結果產生重大影響，並可能導致我們財務狀況及獲利能力惡化。
與我們營運相關之風險
運輸服務或港口設施中斷，以及運輸成本增加，可能會影響我們供應燃煤給客戶的能力，降低需求，並對我們業務產生負面影響。
某些員工福利的支出可能大幅高於我們預期，這可能會增加我們的成本，並對我們的財務結果產生不利影響。
本公司業務需要大量的資本投資及維護支出，而我們可能無法提供這些資金。
paragraphs: 投資於本公司證券會面臨各種風險，包括本公司業務內在的風險與不確定性。如後續頁數所詳述，這些風險包括但不限於以下內容：
•與我們產業及總體經濟相關的風險，例如與低煤價、客戶流失、關稅及其他貿易限制、我們取得融資及其他服務的能力、競爭、煤炭需求減少、客戶信用worthiness及總體經濟中斷相關的風險。
•與法規與法律發展相關的風險，例如與法規要求及成本、醫療保健法規及成本、許可證批准、氣候變遷法規、社會與治理倡議及法規、環境法規與條約、不利的稅務措施、能源需求減少、環境清理成本及內部控制維護相關的風險。
•與我們營運相關的風險，例如與採礦及其他條件相關的風險，許多風險超出我們的控制範圍、運輸服務中斷、具備專業技能勞工的可得性、高於預估的員工福利成本、煤炭儲備的可得性、設備可得性、設備故障、高於預期的財產復原或礦場關閉成本、工會化、網路安全、人工智慧、中央阿巴拉契亞地區採礦的複雜性、我們對第三方的依賴以及我們進行資本投資的能力。
•與我們流動性相關的風險，例如我們取得或更新擔保債券的能力、我們維持所需信用狀（"LCs"）容量的需求、我們借款安排或任何未來債務工具所施加的限制，以及在需要時取得資金的能力。
•與本公司普通股所有權相關的風險，例如與遵守證券法規、本公司普通股順利交易市場的可得性、本公司重購普通股的能力（視董事會決定而定）、發行額外證券所導致的稀釋或其他影響、對第三方收購本公司的障礙以及股東訴訟事項的有限司法管轄範圍。
